What are backup and disaster recovery services?

settings.editor: Backup and disaster recovery services restore data, systems, applications and infrastructure after a disruption.
Having backups is only part of it. The real goal is proof that critical services can be restored within agreed recovery targets.
A complete recovery plan should define:
Which systems are business-critical
How much downtime is acceptable
How much data loss you can tolerate
Where backups are stored
How recovery will be validated
Who is responsible during an incident

settings.title: How tested backups keep business running

settings.editor: Recovery plans focus on the systems, workloads and data your operations depend on.
Backup jobs and recoverability are checked regularly, so problems surface early.
RTO and RPO targets make downtime and data-loss limits clear before an incident.
Recovery strategies cover isolated backups, compromised credentials, clean restores and validation.
Regular recovery exercises prove whether documented plans work when systems fail.
Plans are updated as infrastructure, applications, workloads and business needs change.

settings.editor: Backup Monitoring
A backup job marked "complete" isn't always a backup you can restore. Folio3 managed backup and disaster recovery services check backup activity every day to catch:
Failed or incomplete jobs
Missing recovery points
Backup agent issues
Storage capacity problems
Retention policy gaps
Systems left out of protection
Alerts are reviewed, and unresolved failures are escalated for action.
Outcome
Backup problems found and fixed long before you need to recover.

settings.editor: Recovery Targets

Recovery planning starts with clear targets. Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is how quickly a service must be restored. Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is how much recent data the business can afford to lose.
Folio3 helps set RTO and RPO commitments based on:
Business impact
System criticality
How often data changes
Application dependencies
Recovery technology
Regulatory requirements
Available budget
Outcome
Recovery priorities set by business need, not assumptions.
Keeping every backup in one place puts all of them at risk from a single incident.
Folio3 designs layered backup protection using:
Off-site backup storage
Hosted backup environments
Encrypted data transfer
Retention policies
Immutable backup options
Geographic separation
Access restrictions
The design can follow the 3-2-1 backup rule: three copies of your data, on two types of media, with one copy kept off-site.
Outcome
Stronger protection against site loss and ransomware.

settings.editor: Ransomware Readiness
Ransomware recovery takes more than restoring a few files.
Folio3 prepares you for ransomware incidents by reviewing:
Backup isolation
Immutable recovery points
Privileged access
Recovery order
Containment procedures
Clean restore environments
Communication responsibilities
Recovery testing
Planned exercises confirm that systems can be restored without bringing back infected files or compromised accounts.
Outcome
A tested recovery plan for ransomware attacks.

settings.editor: Continuity Planning
Disaster recovery restores technology. A business continuity plan sets out how your organization keeps operating while systems are down.
Folio3 helps document:
Critical business processes
Recovery priorities
Department responsibilities
Alternative working arrangements
Communication procedures
Technology dependencies
Vendor contacts
Escalation paths
Outcome
Clear steps for keeping essential operations running during a disruption.
